issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s need for possession is not reasonable when the landlord seeks premises that were residential at the relevant starting point for a non-residential use that is prohibited and punishable.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession on the ground that it reasonably and bona fide required the premises for its own purposes.
The premises had been used for residential purposes when the Act came into force.
The landlord sought to use the premises for business activities, including offices, shops, storage, and classes.
The courts below found that the landlord genuinely needed the premises for its business, but the intended uses were non-residential.
The applicable law prohibited using premises that were residential at the relevant starting point for a non-residential purpose and made such use punishable.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s established business need was not reasonable because the intended use ran contrary to a statutory prohibition and could expose the landlord to penal consequences. No decree for possession could be passed, and the suits were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(1)(g) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, a landlord must establish that the premises are reasonably and bona fide required; proof of need alone is insufficient. The reasonableness of the need must be judged in light of all the circumstances, including whether the proposed use is prohibited and punishable under section 25(1) and (2). This does not mean that section 25 overrides section 13(1): even granting section 13(1) priority under its non-obstante clause, its own requirement of reasonableness must be satisfied. Courts should not construe legislation to encourage its breach or grant a decree that, if acted upon, would expose the landlord to penal consequences. The Court approved the approach in Laxmi Cooperative Bank Ltd. v. Mohan Govind Diwanji.

rule.if: possession_claim_on_reasonable_need_ground and premises_residential_at_relevant_start and landlord_sought_nonresidential_use and proposed_use_prohibited_and_punishable

predicates.possession_claim_on_reasonable_need_grou: A landlord sought possession on the ground that the premises were reasonably required for the landlord’s occupation.
predicates.premises_residential_at_relevant_start: The premises were used for residential purposes at the relevant starting point.
predicates.landlord_sought_nonresidential_use: The landlord sought possession to use the premises for a non-residential purpose.
predicates.proposed_use_prohibited_and_punishable: The applicable law prohibited the proposed non-residential use of premises that were residential at the relevant starting point and made that use punishable.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession on a reasonable-need ground for premises that were residential at the relevant starting point, and the landlord’s intended non-residential use is prohibited and punishable, the claimed requirement is not reasonable.
